Earlier this year, Iraq already threatened with leaving the cartel if it didn't get its way. 

https://t.co/u7JDqQXZ61

The market is comfortable assuming that Iran lacks either the ability or the will to escalate further.

“If they can reduce flows, why haven’t they done so already?”

That was one of the questions a trader asked me. And for now, that is the correct sentiment. Iran has not escalated to ship-to-ship zones like Fujairah or Sohar. So from the oil market’s perspective, Iran has already lost, because what they could’ve done should’ve been executed already, but they have not done so.

Now I can sit here and write about how any of that is nonsense or whatever, but the reality is no one knows. No one knows what they are or are not capable of. No one knows what game plan they really have. And truthfully, no one other than the Iranians themselves knows when they will escalate.

Logic tells me this status quo is unsustainable, and the escalation window before year-end would match both the congressional pressure coming down on Trump and the tiny cushion we have left in oil inventories.
